note.S:
CC: I keep getting spells of wheezing and a tight chest.

HPI: 27-year-old female. Six weeks of intermittent wheezing and chest tightness. Diffuse chest tightness. Expiratory wheeze and difficulty exhaling. Interrupts jogging; speech maintained. Episodes 10–20 minutes, approximately 3 days weekly. Weekly nocturnal cough. Flour-dust exposure at bakery; improved during 4 days away. Cold air and cleaning sprays also trigger symptoms. Improves with rest and exposure avoidance. No prior inhaler trial. Childhood allergic rhinitis without prior asthma diagnosis.

PMH: Seasonal allergic rhinitis; occasional heartburn.

PSH: Wisdom teeth removed at 20.

Meds: Cetirizine 10 mg as needed; antacid approximately weekly.

SH: Never smoked or vaped. No alcohol. No recreational drugs. Bakery dough mixing with flour exposure; inconsistent respiratory protection. Lives with two roommates; no household pets or smoke. LMP 2 weeks ago; IUD; pregnancy not suspected by patient.

FH: Mother: asthma; brother: eczema. Father: no known major illness.

Allergies: TMP-SMX: nonblistering rash at 17, no respiratory symptoms.

ROS: Respiratory: Dry nocturnal cough. Episodic dyspnea; none at rest now. No hemoptysis. Heent: Seasonal rhinorrhea. Occasional throat tightness with episodes. Transient postepisode hoarseness. General: No fever. Fatigue after disrupted sleep. No weight loss.
note.O:
Vitals: BP 116/72 mmHg, P 84 bpm, R 18 rpm, T 98.2 F oral, Pulse Ox 98% on room air, Ht 5' 4", Wt 138 lbs

General: Alert, speaking comfortably in full sentences; no respiratory distress.
Heart: Regular rate and rhythm without murmur.
Lungs: Mild bilateral expiratory wheezes with prolonged expiration; no focal crackles.
Lungs: Symmetric chest movement without accessory muscle use.
HEENT: Pale edematous nasal mucosa with clear secretions bilaterally.
HEENT: No tonsillar swelling or exudate; voice clear at rest.
Osteopathic: T3 right paraspinal tissue texture change and tenderness.
P: 1. Arrange pre/post-bronchodilator spirometry; consider serial peak-flow records at and away from work and occupational review. Start an inhaled-corticosteroid-containing plan if asthma is established; teach inhaler technique and an action plan. Arrange temporary duties away from flour exposure pending occupational assessment; review in 2 weeks. Severe breathlessness or inability to speak needs emergency help.

2. If throat/voice episodes persist or lung tests do not explain them, refer for laryngeal assessment during symptoms and breathing retraining. Discuss irritant avoidance and explain overlap with asthma.
3. If reflux symptoms persist, use meal-timing/trigger measures and consider a supervised acid-suppression trial after review. Explain that reflux treatment does not replace respiratory evaluation.

walkthroughs.estimate_method: 150 spoken words/minute plus the full simulation examination durations and 55 seconds for introductions and transitions; explanatory commentary excluded. This is a planning estimate, not a measured student performance.

reasoning.question: Do spells occur at work, away from work, or during sleep?
reasoning.why: Characterize variable obstruction and distinguish lung wheeze from throat symptoms.
reasoning.if_present: Use the reported pattern to select the relevant examinations and assess urgency.
reasoning.if_absent: Keep alternatives open and ask a focused follow-up.
reasoning.document: Separate reported symptoms, observed signs, assessment and proposed care.

differentials.name: Asthma, possibly work-related
differentials.teaching_context: Variable nocturnal/exertional symptoms, atopy and expiratory wheeze support asthma; work association requires evaluation.

differentials.name: Irritant-triggered inducible laryngeal obstruction
differentials.teaching_context: Episodic throat tightness and voice change with irritants support consideration; expiratory wheeze favors asthma and both may coexist.

differentials.name: Gastroesophageal reflux with airway symptoms
differentials.teaching_context: Reported heartburn and nocturnal cough support reflux as a contributor, but do not explain all wheezing.

omissions: Explaining uncertainty and the practical follow-up plan.
